---
title: "ModelArray on a TileDB store in S3: cortical thickness across the sensorimotor-association axis"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
    df_print: paged
params:
  store_uri: "s3://fcp-indi/data/Projects/RBC/RBC_FreeSurfer-Post_ModelArray/rbc_freesurferpost.tdb"
  cohort_url: "https://fcp-indi.s3.amazonaws.com/data/Projects/RBC/RBC_FreeSurfer-Post_ModelArray/rbc_freesurferpost_cohort.csv"
  s3_region: "us-east-1"
  n_cores: 4
  out_dir: "~/rbc_s3_example"
  cache_dir: NULL
  quick: TRUE
  hemispheres: NULL
  parcels: NULL
  max_tiles_per_parcel: NULL
  max_vertices_per_parcel: NULL
  allocation_mb: 512
  max_age: 23
  harmonize: TRUE
  write_cifti: TRUE
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, comment = "#>")
report_started <- Sys.time()

# ---- presets -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Binder gives one core and about 2 GB, so default to the smallest run there.
on_binder <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("BINDER_REPO_URL"))
p <- params
p$out_dir <- path.expand(p$out_dir)
if (is.null(p$cache_dir)) p$cache_dir <- file.path(p$out_dir, "cache")
p$cache_dir <- path.expand(p$cache_dir)
if (on_binder) {
  p$quick <- TRUE
  p$n_cores <- 1L
  p$allocation_mb <- min(p$allocation_mb, 256)
}
if (is.null(p$hemispheres)) p$hemispheres <- if (p$quick) "L" else "LR"
if (is.null(p$parcels)) p$parcels <- c("3b", "46")
if (is.null(p$max_tiles_per_parcel)) p$max_tiles_per_parcel <- if (on_binder) 1L else if (p$quick) 2L else 6L
if (is.null(p$max_vertices_per_parcel)) p$max_vertices_per_parcel <- if (on_binder) 150L else if (p$quick) 300L else 500L
dir.create(p$out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(p$cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- packages ----------------------------------------------------------------
needed <- c("ModelArray", "tiledb", "TileDBArray", "jsonlite", "rhdf5", "mgcv", "ggplot2", "MASS")
missing_pkgs <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop("Please install these packages first: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "),
       ". See vignette('rbc-s3-tiledb') for the install commands.", call. = FALSE)
}
have_combat <- requireNamespace("ComBatFamily", quietly = TRUE)
have_lme4 <- requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
have_gamm4 <- requireNamespace("gamm4", quietly = TRUE)
have_gratia <- requireNamespace("gratia", quietly = TRUE)
have_cowplot <- requireNamespace("cowplot", quietly = TRUE)   # optional: brain-locator insets on the figures
harmonize <- isTRUE(p$harmonize) && have_combat
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ModelArray)
  library(ggplot2)
})
if (!exists(".require_tiledb_support", envir = asNamespace("ModelArray"))) {
  stop("This ModelArray predates TileDB support. Install the current GitHub main (see the vignette).", call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- Connectome Workbench ------------------------------------------------------
wb <- Sys.which("wb_command")
if (!nzchar(wb)) {
  for (candidate in c("/Applications/wb_view.app/Contents/usr/bin/wb_command",
                      "/Applications/ConnectomeWorkbench.app/Contents/usr/bin/wb_command",
                      path.expand("~/.wb/bin/wb_command"))) {
    if (file.exists(candidate)) { wb <- candidate; break }
  }
}
have_wb <- nzchar(wb) && isTRUE(p$write_cifti)
wb_run <- function(...) {
  out <- system2(wb, c(...), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(attr(out, "status")) && attr(out, "status") != 0) {
    stop("wb_command failed:\n", paste(out, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(out)
}

# ---- TileDB read settings and helpers ----------------------------------------
# tiledb's R package reads a query in passes sized by this preference (10 MiB by
# default). Each pass re-fetches the tiles it touches, so a read of a few tiles can
# download them six times over. One pass per parcel read needs about 67 MB per tile.
tiledb::set_allocation_size_preference(as.integer(p$allocation_mb) * 1024^2)
TILE_ROWS <- 964L                      # vertices per tile in this store
N_SESSIONS <- 8696L
TILE_MB <- TILE_ROWS * N_SESSIONS * 4 / 1024^2
tile_of <- function(i) (as.integer(i) - 1L) %/% TILE_ROWS   # 1-based element -> 0-based tile

runtime <- data.frame(step = character(), secs = numeric(), tiles = numeric(),
                      mb_uncompressed = numeric(), mb_wire = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stat_value <- function(raw, key) {
  m <- regmatches(raw, regexpr(sprintf('"%s": *[0-9.]+', key), raw))
  if (length(m) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(sub(".*: *", "", m))
}
# Run expr with TileDB statistics on, and record time, tiles and bytes for the table.
tdb_measure <- function(step, expr) {
  tiledb::tiledb_stats_reset()
  tiledb::tiledb_stats_enable()
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  value <- force(expr)
  secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")
  raw <- paste(suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(tiledb::tiledb_stats_raw_get())), collapse = "")
  tiledb::tiledb_stats_disable()
  runtime[nrow(runtime) + 1, ] <<- list(step, secs,
    stat_value(raw, "Context.Query.Reader.num_tiles_read"),
    stat_value(raw, "Context.Query.Reader.read_unfiltered_byte_num") / 1024^2,
    stat_value(raw, "Context.VFS.read_byte_num") / 1024^2)
  value
}
# Time a local computation (no S3 traffic) into the same table.
timed <- function(step, expr) {
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  value <- force(expr)
  runtime[nrow(runtime) + 1, ] <<- list(step, as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"), NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_)
  value
}
last_runtime <- function() runtime[nrow(runtime), ]
cached_download <- function(url, name = basename(url)) {
  if (file.exists(url)) return(url)                # a local file was given instead of a URL
  dest <- file.path(p$cache_dir, name)
  if (!file.exists(dest) || file.size(dest) == 0) {
    utils::download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }
  dest
}
fmt_secs <- function(s) if (s < 90) sprintf("%.1f s", s) else sprintf("%.1f min", s / 60)
```

This report fits models to the [Reproducible Brain Charts](https://reprobrainchart.github.io/)
FreeSurferPost cortical thickness data **without downloading the dataset**. The data
live in a 553 GB TileDB store on a public S3 bucket; ModelArray reads only the pieces
it needs. The question is one with a known answer, so you can judge the result:

> The cortex thins through childhood and adolescence, but not everywhere at the same
> time. Primary sensory and motor cortex matures first: its thinning is mostly over by
> mid-adolescence. Association cortex matures last: it keeps thinning through the teens
> and into the twenties. This example contrasts two parcels at opposite ends of the
> sensorimotor–association (S-A) axis of Sydnor et al. (2021): area **3b**, primary
> somatosensory cortex (S-A rank 7), and area **46**, dorsolateral prefrontal
> association cortex (S-A rank 174). 3b should do most of its thinning early and flatten
> by mid-adolescence; 46 should still be thinning in the late teens and twenties.

Settings for this run: `quick = `r p$quick``, hemispheres `r p$hemispheres`, parcels
`r paste(p$parcels, collapse = ", ")`, at most `r p$max_tiles_per_parcel` tile(s) and
`r p$max_vertices_per_parcel` vertices per parcel, ages up to `r p$max_age` for the
vertex-wise models, `r p$n_cores` core(s), site harmonization
`r if (harmonize) "on (CovBat)" else "off (site as a covariate)"`.
`r if (on_binder) "Running on Binder, so the smallest settings are used." else ""`

## 1. Point TileDB at the bucket

ModelArray talks to TileDB through the package's default *context*. Two settings make
the public bucket readable: the region, and "do not sign requests" (no AWS account
needed). Set them once, before `ModelArray()`.

```{r tiledb-context}
cfg <- tiledb::tiledb_config()
cfg["vfs.s3.region"] <- p$s3_region
cfg["vfs.s3.no_sign_request"] <- "true"
tiledb::tiledb_ctx(cfg)

reachable <- tryCatch(tiledb::tiledb_vfs_is_dir(p$store_uri, tiledb::tiledb_vfs()), error = function(e) e)
if (!isTRUE(reachable)) {
  cat("Could not reach", p$store_uri, "\n",
      if (inherits(reachable, "error")) conditionMessage(reachable) else "", "\n",
      "Check your network and proxy settings, or try again later.\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

The same two settings can come from environment variables instead
(`TILEDB_VFS_S3_REGION`, `TILEDB_VFS_S3_NO_SIGN_REQUEST`), which is what the Binder
image does.

## 2. What is in the store

`ModelArraySummary()` lists the scalars without loading any data. Every scalar is a
dense matrix of 327,684 fsLR-164k vertices by 8,696 sessions, stored in tiles of
`r TILE_ROWS` vertices × all sessions (about `r round(TILE_MB)` MB each before
compression). Reading one vertex means reading its whole tile; that is the unit all
the costs below are counted in.

```{r summary}
info <- tdb_measure("ModelArraySummary (70 scalars)", ModelArraySummary(p$store_uri))
cat(sprintf("%d scalars, each %d vertices x %d sessions; %s\n",
            nrow(info$scalars), info$scalars$nElements[1], info$scalars$nInputFiles[1],
            fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs)))
print(info$scalars$name)
```

## 3. The cohort

The cohort CSV sits next to the store. It is long format (one row per session per
scalar), so we keep the `thickness` rows: one per session, with age, sex and scanning
site. Sessions without a sex or site (some HBN sessions) keep an empty value; models
and harmonization skip them where they need the column.

```{r cohort}
cohort_file <- cached_download(p$cohort_url, "rbc_freesurferpost_cohort.csv")
cohort <- read.csv(cohort_file, na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
phen <- cohort[cohort$scalar_name == "thickness", ]
phen$subject <- paste(phen$dataset, phen$subject_id)
have_covariates <- all(c("sex", "site") %in% names(phen))
if (have_covariates) {
  phen$sex <- factor(phen$sex)
  phen$site <- factor(phen$site)
} else {
  cat("This cohort file has no sex/site columns yet; using the study (dataset) as the batch variable.\n")
  phen$site <- factor(phen$dataset)
  phen$sex <- factor(rep("unknown", nrow(phen)))
}
use_sex <- nlevels(phen$sex) > 1
sex_term <- if (use_sex) " + sex" else ""
site_term <- if (nlevels(phen$site) > 1) " + site" else ""
harmonize_covariates <- c("Age", if (use_sex) "sex")

by_study <- split(phen, phen$dataset)
sessions <- data.frame(
  dataset = names(by_study),
  sessions = vapply(by_study, nrow, integer(1)),
  subjects = vapply(by_study, function(d) length(unique(d$subject)), integer(1)),
  age_min = vapply(by_study, function(d) round(min(d$Age), 1), numeric(1)),
  age_max = vapply(by_study, function(d) round(max(d$Age), 1), numeric(1)),
  no_sex = vapply(by_study, function(d) sum(is.na(d$sex)), integer(1)),
  no_site = vapply(by_study, function(d) sum(is.na(d$site)), integer(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
sessions
cat(sprintf("%d sessions, %d subjects, %d sites\n", nrow(phen), length(unique(phen$subject)), nlevels(phen$site)))
```

## 4. Open the store

Only the scalar we name gets opened; nothing is read yet. The `curv` scalar would be a
natural second covariate, but ModelArray attaches a second scalar only when it lists
the same source files as the phenotypes, and in this store each scalar has its own
file per session. So the models here use `thickness` alone.

```{r open}
ma <- tdb_measure("ModelArray() open", ModelArray(p$store_uri, scalar_types = "thickness"))
ma
src <- sources(ma)[["thickness"]]
stopifnot(setequal(src, phen$source_file))
phen <- phen[match(src, phen$source_file), ]           # same order as the store's columns
cat(sprintf("Opened in %s\n", fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs)))
```

## 5. Parcels and tiles

A Glasser (HCP-MMP1.0) label for each of the 327,684 columns ships with the example,
together with each parcel's S-A rank. Before reading anything we can count how many
tiles a parcel touches. fsLR numbers its vertices in nested rings, so a parcel's
vertices are spread over many tiles; the report keeps the vertices in each parcel's
most populated tiles, which caps the download while keeping hundreds of vertices.

```{r atlas}
labels <- readRDS(system.file("examples/rbc-s3-tiledb/glasser360_fsLR164k_labels.rds", package = "ModelArray"))
stopifnot(length(labels$key) == nrow(scalars(ma)[["thickness"]]))
ladder <- labels$table[labels$table$region %in% p$parcels & labels$table$hemi %in% strsplit(p$hemispheres, "")[[1]], ]
ladder <- ladder[order(ladder$sa_rank, ladder$hemi), ]

pick_vertices <- function(key) {
  idx <- which(labels$key == key)
  tiles <- sort(table(tile_of(idx)), decreasing = TRUE)
  keep_tiles <- as.integer(names(tiles))[seq_len(min(p$max_tiles_per_parcel, length(tiles)))]
  idx <- idx[tile_of(idx) %in% keep_tiles]
  if (length(idx) > p$max_vertices_per_parcel) {
    set.seed(2026)
    idx <- sort(sample(idx, p$max_vertices_per_parcel))
  }
  list(idx = idx, n_all = sum(tiles), n_tiles_all = length(tiles), tiles = sort(keep_tiles))
}
selection <- lapply(ladder$key, pick_vertices)
names(selection) <- ladder$name
ladder$vertices_in_parcel <- vapply(selection, function(s) s$n_all, numeric(1))
ladder$tiles_in_parcel <- vapply(selection, function(s) s$n_tiles_all, numeric(1))
ladder$tiles_read <- vapply(selection, function(s) length(s$tiles), numeric(1))
ladder$vertices_used <- vapply(selection, function(s) length(s$idx), numeric(1))
ladder$predicted_mb <- round(ladder$tiles_read * TILE_MB)
ladder[, c("name", "sa_rank", "vertices_in_parcel", "tiles_in_parcel", "tiles_read", "vertices_used", "predicted_mb")]
```

## 6. Where the two parcels sit on the brain

The two parcels sit at opposite ends of the sensorimotor–association (S-A) axis of
Sydnor et al. (2021). The figure below is that axis on the left inflated cortex, in
Sydnor's colour scheme (Figure 2A): gold at the sensorimotor pole (low rank), through
white, to purple at the association pole (high rank). Area 3b (rank 7) is deep in the
gold sensorimotor end; area 46 (rank 174) is deep in the purple association end. Every
figure below colours the two parcels by these same S-A colours, so a parcel's colour
tells you where it sits on the axis. The brain image ships with the example and is a
left-lateral view (right-hemisphere parcels are shown at their left-hemisphere homolog).

```{r fig-helpers}
# Sydnor et al. 2021 (Neuron) Fig 2A S-A colour scheme: gold (sensorimotor) -> white -> purple (association)
SA_COLS <- c("goldenrod1", "white", "#6f1282"); SA_MID <- 90; SA_RANGE <- c(1, 180)
sa_rank_col <- function(r) scales::gradient_n_pal(SA_COLS)(scales::rescale_mid(r, to = c(0, 1), from = SA_RANGE, mid = SA_MID))
parcel_regions <- unique(ladder$region[order(ladder$sa_rank)])
parcel_ranks <- vapply(parcel_regions, function(rg) ladder$sa_rank[ladder$region == rg][1], numeric(1))
parcel_cols <- stats::setNames(sa_rank_col(parcel_ranks), parcel_regions)

# The shipped S-A brains, as overlay grobs: "axis" (3b and 46 outlined and labelled) and
# one per parcel ("3b", "46", outlined only) for the per-panel locators.
brain_files <- c(axis = "brain_sa_axis.png", "3b" = "brain_sa_3b.png", "46" = "brain_sa_46.png")
brain_paths <- vapply(brain_files, function(f) system.file(file.path("examples/rbc-s3-tiledb", f), package = "ModelArray"), character(1))
have_brain <- have_cowplot && all(nzchar(brain_paths)) && requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)
brain_grobs <- if (have_brain) lapply(brain_paths, function(p) grid::rasterGrob(png::readPNG(p), interpolate = TRUE)) else NULL
add_brain <- function(plot, which = "axis", x = 0.0, y = 0.6, w = 0.3, h = 0.3) {
  if (!have_brain) return(plot)
  cowplot::ggdraw(plot) + cowplot::draw_grob(brain_grobs[[which]], x = x, y = y, width = w, height = h)
}
```

```{r sa-axis-figure, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3}
if (have_brain) {
  bar <- data.frame(rank = SA_RANGE[1]:SA_RANGE[2])
  ticks <- data.frame(rank = parcel_ranks, lab = parcel_regions)
  colourbar <- ggplot(bar, aes(rank, 1, fill = rank)) + geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = SA_COLS[1], mid = SA_COLS[2], high = SA_COLS[3], midpoint = SA_MID, guide = "none") +
    geom_point(data = ticks, aes(rank, 1), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 25, size = 2.4, fill = "black") +
    geom_text(data = ticks, aes(rank, 1.9, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE, fontface = 2, size = 3.4) +
    annotate("text", x = SA_RANGE[1], y = -1.2, label = "sensorimotor", hjust = 0, size = 3.2) +
    annotate("text", x = SA_RANGE[2], y = -1.2, label = "association", hjust = 1, size = 3.2) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 2.8)) + theme_void()
  print(cowplot::plot_grid(cowplot::ggdraw() + cowplot::draw_grob(brain_grobs[["axis"]]),
                           colourbar, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(3, 1)))
} else {
  cat("Install cowplot and png to show the S-A axis brain figure.\n")
}
```

## 7. One vertex at a time

`exampleElementData()` returns the data frame a per-vertex model sees: the cohort plus
that vertex's values. We take one vertex near the middle of the lower-ranked parcel
(3b) and one near the middle of the higher-ranked parcel (46). The medial wall is
stored as zeros, which is a handy check that the labels line up with the data.

```{r vertex-data}
mid_vertex <- function(sel) sel$idx[which.min(abs(sel$idx - median(sel$idx)))]
low_name <- names(selection)[which.min(ladder$sa_rank)]
top_name <- names(selection)[which.max(ladder$sa_rank)]
v_low <- mid_vertex(selection[[low_name]])
v_top <- mid_vertex(selection[[top_name]])
low_region <- ladder$region[ladder$name == low_name]; low_rank <- ladder$sa_rank[ladder$name == low_name]
top_region <- ladder$region[ladder$name == top_name]; top_rank <- ladder$sa_rank[ladder$name == top_name]

# a medial-wall vertex in a tile we will read anyway, if there is one; otherwise the nearest one
tiles_planned <- unique(unlist(lapply(selection, `[[`, "tiles")))
wall_all <- which(labels$key == 0L)
wall_in_plan <- wall_all[tile_of(wall_all) %in% tiles_planned]
wall <- if (length(wall_in_plan)) wall_in_plan[1] else wall_all[which.min(abs(wall_all - v_low))]
n_tiles <- length(unique(tile_of(c(v_low, wall))))

two <- tdb_measure(sprintf("1 %s vertex + 1 medial-wall vertex (%d tile%s)", low_region, n_tiles, if (n_tiles > 1) "s" else ""),
                   as.matrix(scalars(ma)[["thickness"]][c(v_low, wall), ]))
cat(sprintf("%s vertex %d: mean thickness %.2f mm; medial-wall vertex %d: all zero = %s (%s, %.0f MB)\n",
            low_region, v_low, mean(two[1, ]), wall, all(two[2, ] == 0), fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs), last_runtime()$mb_wire))

df_top <- exampleElementData(ma, scalar = "thickness", i_element = v_top, phenotypes = phen)
df_low <- exampleElementData(ma, scalar = "thickness", i_element = v_low, phenotypes = phen)
str(df_top[, c("dataset", "Age", "sex", "site", "thickness")])
```

```{r vertex-figure, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
low_lab <- sprintf("%s (S-A rank %s)", low_region, low_rank)
top_lab <- sprintf("%s (S-A rank %s)", top_region, top_rank)
both <- rbind(cbind(df_low, parcel = low_lab), cbind(df_top, parcel = top_lab))
both$parcel <- factor(both$parcel, levels = c(low_lab, top_lab))
fig1 <- ggplot(both, aes(Age, thickness)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = dataset), alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 4), colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~parcel) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Cortical thickness (mm)", colour = "Study",
       title = sprintf("Thickness against age at one vertex in each parcel (all %s sessions)", format(nrow(phen), big.mark = ","))) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
# a small brain to the left of each panel's title: 3b by the 3b panel, 46 by the 46 panel
if (have_brain && all(c(low_region, top_region) %in% names(brain_grobs))) {
  fig1 <- cowplot::ggdraw(fig1) +
    cowplot::draw_grob(brain_grobs[[low_region]], x = 0.10, y = 0.80, width = 0.11, height = 0.15) +
    cowplot::draw_grob(brain_grobs[[top_region]], x = 0.47, y = 0.80, width = 0.11, height = 0.15)
}
fig1
ggsave(file.path(p$out_dir, "fig1_vertex_thickness_vs_age.png"), fig1, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
```

A plain GAM at the area-`r top_region` vertex over the whole age range, with site as
a covariate, shows the lifespan picture: thickness peaks in early childhood and
declines from then on (Bethlehem et al., 2022), so the slope should be negative in
old age too (ages above 23 come from NKI only). Two checks go with it: the derivative
of the age curve computed two ways, and a mixed model that treats repeat sessions
(two waves in BHRC, several in NKI) properly, which the vertex-wise GAM does not.

```{r vertex-gam}
AGE_GRID <- seq(5, 85, by = 0.5)

# Slope of the age smooth by central finite differences, with a simultaneous 95%
# interval from posterior simulation (the same construction as gratia::derivatives()).
smooth_derivative <- function(fit, newdata, var = "Age", eps = 0.05, nsim = 1000) {
  lo <- newdata; lo[[var]] <- newdata[[var]] - eps
  hi <- newdata; hi[[var]] <- newdata[[var]] + eps
  X <- (predict(fit, hi, type = "lpmatrix") - predict(fit, lo, type = "lpmatrix")) / (2 * eps)
  X[, !grepl(paste0("s(", var, ")"), colnames(X), fixed = TRUE)] <- 0
  b <- coef(fit)
  Vb <- vcov(fit)
  d <- drop(X %*% b)
  se <- sqrt(rowSums((X %*% Vb) * X))
  sims <- X %*% t(MASS::mvrnorm(nsim, b, Vb))
  crit <- stats::quantile(apply(abs(sims - d) / se, 2, max), 0.95)
  data.frame(Age = newdata[[var]], derivative = d, lower = d - crit * se, upper = d + crit * se)
}
# A data frame of typical covariate values (most common level of each factor) along the age grid.
typical_newdata <- function(d, cov_cols, ages = AGE_GRID) {
  ref <- d[1, cov_cols, drop = FALSE]
  for (v in setdiff(cov_cols, "Age")) {
    ref[[v]] <- factor(names(which.max(table(d[[v]]))), levels = levels(d[[v]]))
  }
  nd <- ref[rep(1, length(ages)), , drop = FALSE]
  nd$Age <- ages
  nd
}

d_demo <- df_top[stats::complete.cases(df_top[, c("thickness", "Age", "sex", "site")]), ]
d_demo$site <- droplevels(d_demo$site)
f_demo <- stats::as.formula(paste0("thickness ~ s(Age, k = 4)", sex_term, site_term))
fit_demo <- mgcv::gam(f_demo, data = d_demo, method = "REML")
summary(fit_demo)$s.table
nd_demo <- typical_newdata(d_demo, c("Age", if (use_sex) "sex", if (nzchar(site_term)) "site"))
deriv_demo <- smooth_derivative(fit_demo, nd_demo)
cat(sprintf("Mean slope 8-22: %.1f microns/yr; 60-80: %.1f microns/yr\n",
            1000 * mean(deriv_demo$derivative[deriv_demo$Age >= 8 & deriv_demo$Age <= 22]),
            1000 * mean(deriv_demo$derivative[deriv_demo$Age >= 60 & deriv_demo$Age <= 80])))
if (have_gratia) {
  g <- gratia::derivatives(fit_demo, select = "s(Age)", n = 50, interval = "simultaneous")
  ours <- smooth_derivative(fit_demo, typical_newdata(d_demo, names(nd_demo), ages = g$Age))
  cat(sprintf("Derivative check against gratia::derivatives(): max |difference| = %.1e mm/yr\n", max(abs(ours$derivative - g$.derivative))))
}
if (have_lme4) {
  f_mixed <- stats::as.formula(paste0("thickness ~ Age", sex_term, site_term, " + (1 | subject)"))
  mixed <- lme4::lmer(f_mixed, data = d_demo)
  cat(sprintf("Mixed model (%d subjects with repeat sessions): linear age slope = %.1f microns/yr (SE %.1f)\n",
              sum(table(d_demo$subject) > 1), 1000 * lme4::fixef(mixed)[["Age"]], 1000 * sqrt(diag(as.matrix(vcov(mixed))))[["Age"]]))
}
```

## 8. Pull each parcel from S3 and harmonize it

Nine scanning sites contributed, and they differ in the mean and the spread of
thickness, so a `site` covariate removes only part of the difference. CovBat
(`ComBatFamily::covfam()`) harmonizes mean, variance and the covariance between
features across sites while keeping the age and sex effects (`y ~ s(Age, k = 4) + sex`).
Its features here are the vertices of a parcel, read from S3 in one go: that is
what the method is built for, and it is far cheaper than harmonizing vertex by vertex.

The raw and harmonized blocks go into a small local ModelArray store, one row per
selected vertex, so that the per-vertex models in section 8 run with the usual
ModelArray functions. Nothing is written back to S3.

```{r parcel-harmonize}
local_h5 <- file.path(p$out_dir, "rbc_parcels_local.h5")
if (file.exists(local_h5)) unlink(local_h5)
write_local_scalar <- function(file, name, mat, column_names) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) rhdf5::h5createFile(file)
  if (!"scalars" %in% rhdf5::h5ls(file, recursive = FALSE)$name) rhdf5::h5createGroup(file, "scalars")
  rhdf5::h5createGroup(file, paste0("scalars/", name))
  # one row (element) per chunk: ModelArray reads elements one at a time
  rhdf5::h5createDataset(file, paste0("scalars/", name, "/values"), dims = dim(mat), storage.mode = "double",
                         chunk = c(1L, ncol(mat)), level = 4L)
  rhdf5::h5write(mat, file, paste0("scalars/", name, "/values"))
  rhdf5::h5write(column_names, file, paste0("scalars/", name, "/column_names"))
  rhdf5::h5closeAll()
}

# Read one parcel at a time, so each read can be checked against the tile prediction
raw_blocks <- list(); elements <- list()
for (nm in names(selection)) {
  sel <- selection[[nm]]
  block <- tdb_measure(sprintf("read %s (%d vertices, %d tile%s)", nm, length(sel$idx), length(sel$tiles), if (length(sel$tiles) > 1) "s" else ""),
                       as.matrix(scalars(ma)[["thickness"]][sel$idx, ]))
  r <- last_runtime()
  cat(sprintf("%-12s %4d vertices  %5.1f s  tiles read %2.0f (predicted %2d) %s  %4.0f MB on the wire\n",
              nm, nrow(block), r$secs, r$tiles, length(sel$tiles),
              if (is.na(r$tiles) || r$tiles <= length(sel$tiles)) "PASS" else "FAIL", r$mb_wire))
  usable <- apply(block, 1, function(v) all(is.finite(v)) && stats::sd(v) > 0)
  raw_blocks[[nm]] <- block[usable, , drop = FALSE]
  elements[[nm]] <- data.frame(vertex = sel$idx[usable], name = nm, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
```

CovBat fits one GAM per vertex and keeps every fit. Each fit carries copies of the
data (about 5 MB at this sample size) that `covfam()` never uses again, so
`slim_gam()` drops them; the harmonized values are identical. Parcels are harmonized
independently, so they can run at the same time, one per core (forked processes;
on Windows they run one after another). Each worker needs about 1 GB per 300 vertices.

```{r parcel-covbat}
ok_batch <- stats::complete.cases(phen[, c("site", harmonize_covariates)])
d_batch <- droplevels(phen[ok_batch, , drop = FALSE])
slim_gam <- function(...) {
  fit <- mgcv::gam(...)
  fit[c("call", "model", "y", "fitted.values", "residuals", "linear.predictors", "weights", "prior.weights",
        "working.weights", "hat", "offset", "R", "qrx", "db.drho", "dw.drho", "F")] <- NULL
  fit
}
covbat_block <- function(block) {
  h <- suppressWarnings(ComBatFamily::covfam(
    data = t(block[, ok_batch, drop = FALSE]), bat = d_batch$site,
    covar = d_batch[, harmonize_covariates, drop = FALSE], model = slim_gam,
    formula = stats::as.formula(paste0("y ~ s(Age, k = 4)", sex_term)), eb = TRUE))
  harm <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(block), ncol(block))
  harm[, ok_batch] <- t(as.matrix(h$dat.covbat))
  harm
}
covbat_cores <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else max(1L, min(as.integer(p$n_cores), length(raw_blocks)))
if (harmonize) {
  harm_blocks <- timed(sprintf("CovBat, %d parcels on %d core%s", length(raw_blocks), covbat_cores, if (covbat_cores > 1) "s" else ""),
    if (covbat_cores > 1) {
      parallel::mclapply(raw_blocks, covbat_block, mc.cores = covbat_cores, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
    } else {
      lapply(raw_blocks, covbat_block)
    })
  failed <- vapply(harm_blocks, function(x) inherits(x, "try-error") || is.null(x), logical(1))
  if (any(failed)) {
    stop("CovBat failed for ", paste(names(harm_blocks)[failed], collapse = ", "), ": ",
         paste(unique(vapply(harm_blocks[failed], function(x) if (is.null(x)) "worker returned nothing (out of memory?)" else as.character(x), "")), collapse = "; "),
         "\nTry a smaller n_cores or max_vertices_per_parcel.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  cat(sprintf("CovBat on %d sessions x %d vertices (%d parcels, %d core%s) in %s\n", sum(ok_batch), sum(vapply(raw_blocks, nrow, integer(1))),
              length(raw_blocks), covbat_cores, if (covbat_cores > 1) "s" else "", fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs)))
} else {
  harm_blocks <- lapply(raw_blocks, function(b) matrix(NA_real_, nrow(b), ncol(b)))
}

elements <- do.call(rbind, elements)
elements$element_id <- seq_len(nrow(elements)) - 1L               # ModelArray's 0-based ids in the local store
elements <- merge(elements, ladder[, c("name", "hemi", "region", "sa_rank")], by = "name", sort = FALSE)
elements <- elements[order(elements$element_id), c("element_id", "vertex", "name", "hemi", "region", "sa_rank")]
rownames(elements) <- NULL
write_local_scalar(local_h5, "thickness_raw", do.call(rbind, raw_blocks), src)
if (harmonize) write_local_scalar(local_h5, "thickness_covbat", do.call(rbind, harm_blocks), src)
utils::write.csv(elements, file.path(p$out_dir, "elements.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nLocal store %s: %d vertices x %d sessions, %.0f MB\n", basename(local_h5), nrow(elements), length(src), file.size(local_h5) / 1024^2))
```

```{r site-figure, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
if (harmonize) {
  row_top <- match(v_top, elements$vertex[elements$name == top_name])
  dh <- data.frame(site = phen$site, Age = phen$Age,
                   raw = raw_blocks[[top_name]][row_top, ],
                   harmonized = harm_blocks[[top_name]][row_top, ])
  dh <- dh[ok_batch, ]
  dh$site <- droplevels(dh$site)
  site_stats <- data.frame(site = levels(dh$site),
                           n = as.vector(table(dh$site)),
                           mean_raw = round(tapply(dh$raw, dh$site, mean), 3),
                           sd_raw = round(tapply(dh$raw, dh$site, sd), 3),
                           mean_harmonized = round(tapply(dh$harmonized, dh$site, mean), 3),
                           sd_harmonized = round(tapply(dh$harmonized, dh$site, sd), 3), row.names = NULL)
  site_stats
  long <- rbind(data.frame(site = dh$site, thickness = dh$raw, stage = "raw"),
                data.frame(site = dh$site, thickness = dh$harmonized, stage = "CovBat-harmonized"))
  long$stage <- factor(long$stage, levels = c("raw", "CovBat-harmonized"))
  fig_sites <- ggplot(long, aes(site, thickness, fill = site)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) + facet_wrap(~stage) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3", guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Thickness (mm)",
         title = sprintf("Area %s vertex %d: thickness by site, before and after harmonization", top_region, v_top)) +
    theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
  fig_sites
  ggsave(file.path(p$out_dir, "fig_site_boxplots.png"), fig_sites, width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 150)
} else {
  cat("Harmonization is off (ComBatFamily not installed or harmonize = FALSE); site enters the models as a covariate.\n")
}
```

Site means still differ a little after harmonization because the age and sex mix
differs between sites, and those effects are kept on purpose.

## 9. Models at every vertex

The developmental question is about ages 5–`r p$max_age`, which is where four of the
five studies sit. ModelArray needs the phenotype table to list every session in the
store, so instead of dropping the older sessions we blank their age; `mgcv` then
leaves them out of every fit.

### The built-in GAM runner, from S3 and from the local store

`ModelArray.gam()` fits a GAM at every element. First straight from S3 on one parcel,
with site as a covariate (no harmonization); then on the local store for every parcel,
on the raw and on the harmonized values. `changed.rsq.term.index = 1` adds the partial
R² of the age smooth. The three runs give a feel for what harmonization changes.
(The S3 run reads more tiles than section 7 did for the same vertices: each worker
fetches its own block of elements, so a tile shared between workers is fetched more
than once. When a block fits in memory, reading it once yourself is cheaper.)

```{r parcel-gam}
phen_dev <- phen
phen_dev$Age[phen_dev$Age > p$max_age] <- NA
cat(sprintf("%d of %d sessions are aged %s or younger\n", sum(!is.na(phen_dev$Age)), nrow(phen_dev), p$max_age))

gam_args <- list(changed.rsq.term.index = list(1), method = "REML", n_cores = p$n_cores,
                 on_error = "skip", pbar = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
demo_name <- names(selection)[1]
demo_idx <- elements$vertex[elements$name == demo_name]
gam_s3 <- tdb_measure(sprintf("ModelArray.gam from S3: %s (%d vertices)", demo_name, length(demo_idx)),
  do.call(ModelArray.gam, c(list(stats::as.formula(paste0("thickness ~ s(Age, k = 4)", sex_term, site_term)),
                                 ma, phen_dev, "thickness", element.subset = as.integer(demo_idx)), gam_args)))
cat(sprintf("S3, %s: %d vertices in %s (%.0f tiles)\n", demo_name, nrow(gam_s3), fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs), last_runtime()$tiles))

local_scalars <- c("thickness_raw", if (harmonize) "thickness_covbat")
ma_local <- ModelArray(local_h5, scalar_types = local_scalars)
ma_local
gam_local <- list()
for (sc in local_scalars) {
  f <- stats::as.formula(paste0(sc, " ~ s(Age, k = 4)", sex_term, if (sc == "thickness_raw") site_term))
  gam_local[[sc]] <- timed(sprintf("ModelArray.gam local: %s (%d vertices)", sc, nrow(elements)),
    do.call(ModelArray.gam, c(list(f, ma_local, phen_dev, sc), gam_args)))
  cat(sprintf("local, %s: %d vertices in %s\n", sc, nrow(gam_local[[sc]]), fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs)))
}

gam_summary <- function(res, label) {
  rsq <- intersect(c("s_Age.partial.rsq", "s_Age.delta.adj.rsq"), names(res))[1]
  data.frame(run = label, vertices = nrow(res),
             pct_fdr_sig = round(100 * mean(res$s_Age.p.value.fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
             median_F = round(median(res$s_Age.statistic, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
             median_partial_rsq = round(median(res[[rsq]], na.rm = TRUE), 4))
}
demo_rows <- elements$element_id[elements$name == demo_name]
rbind(gam_summary(gam_s3, sprintf("S3, raw + site covariate (%s)", demo_name)),
      do.call(rbind, lapply(local_scalars, function(sc)
        gam_summary(gam_local[[sc]][gam_local[[sc]]$element_id %in% demo_rows, ],
                    sprintf("local, %s%s (%s)", sc, if (sc == "thickness_raw") " + site covariate" else "", demo_name)))))
```

### A custom per-vertex function with `ModelArray.wrap()`

`fit_vertex()` adds what `ModelArray.gam()` does not report: a test statistic from an
`fx = TRUE` refit (penalized p-values can be optimistic), ΔR²adj from a reduced model,
predicted thickness every two years, and the slope of the age curve with a simultaneous
95% interval. From the slope it takes the mean thinning rate over 8–22, the age at
which thinning is fastest, the last age at which the slope is still clearly negative,
and the **late fraction**: the share of the 8–22 thinning that happens after age 14.
One row of numbers per vertex.

```{r fit-fun}
response_scalar <- if (harmonize) "thickness_covbat" else "thickness_raw"
DEV_GRID <- seq(5, p$max_age, by = 0.5)
PRED_AGES <- seq(6, 22, by = 2)
fit_vertex <- function(data) {
  d <- data
  d$y <- d[[response_scalar]]
  cov_cols <- c("Age", if (use_sex) "sex", if (!harmonize && nzchar(site_term)) "site")
  d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d[, c("y", cov_cols)]), ]
  for (v in setdiff(cov_cols, "Age")) d[[v]] <- droplevels(d[[v]])
  rhs <- if (length(cov_cols) > 1) paste(cov_cols[-1], collapse = " + ") else "1"
  fit <- mgcv::gam(stats::as.formula(paste("y ~ s(Age, k = 4) +", rhs)), data = d, method = "REML")
  fit_fx <- mgcv::gam(stats::as.formula(paste("y ~ s(Age, k = 4, fx = TRUE) +", rhs)), data = d, method = "REML")
  fit_red <- mgcv::gam(stats::as.formula(paste("y ~", rhs)), data = d, method = "REML")
  s_pen <- summary(fit)$s.table
  s_fx <- summary(fit_fx)$s.table

  newdata <- typical_newdata(d, cov_cols, ages = DEV_GRID)
  pred <- predict(fit, newdata[match(PRED_AGES, DEV_GRID), , drop = FALSE])
  names(pred) <- PRED_AGES
  deriv <- smooth_derivative(fit, newdata)
  in_range <- function(a, b) deriv$Age >= a & deriv$Age <= b
  sig_ages <- deriv$Age[deriv$upper < 0]
  out <- data.frame(
    n = nrow(d),
    edf = unname(s_pen[1, "edf"]),
    F_fx = unname(s_fx[1, "F"]),
    p_fx = unname(s_fx[1, "p-value"]),
    p_pen = unname(s_pen[1, "p-value"]),
    delta_adj_rsq = summary(fit)$r.sq - summary(fit_red)$r.sq,
    rate_8_22 = mean(deriv$derivative[in_range(8, 22)]),
    rate_8_14 = mean(deriv$derivative[in_range(8, 14)]),
    rate_14_22 = mean(deriv$derivative[in_range(14, 22)]),
    late_fraction = unname((pred["14"] - pred["22"]) / (pred["8"] - pred["22"])),
    age_fastest = deriv$Age[which.min(deriv$derivative)],
    thinning_until = if (length(sig_ages)) max(sig_ages) else NA_real_,
    sex_estimate = if (use_sex) unname(coef(fit)[grep("^sex", names(coef(fit)))[1]]) else NA_real_
  )
  out[paste0("pred_", PRED_AGES)] <- as.list(unname(pred))
  out[paste0("slope_", PRED_AGES)] <- as.list(deriv$derivative[match(PRED_AGES, deriv$Age)])
  out
}

# Try it on one element the way ModelArray.wrap() will call it
one <- exampleElementData(ma_local, scalar = response_scalar, i_element = which(elements$vertex == v_top), phenotypes = phen_dev)
round(t(fit_vertex(one)), 4)
check <- analyseOneElement.wrap(which(elements$vertex == v_top), fit_vertex, ma_local, phen_dev, response_scalar,
                                num.subj.lthr = 10, flag_initiate = TRUE, on_error = "stop")
check$column_names
```

```{r parcel-wrap}
vertex_results <- timed(sprintf("ModelArray.wrap fit_vertex (%d vertices)", nrow(elements)),
  ModelArray.wrap(fit_vertex, ma_local, phen_dev, response_scalar, n_cores = p$n_cores,
                  on_error = "skip", pbar = FALSE, verbose = FALSE))
cat(sprintf("%d vertices in %s (%.2f s per vertex per core)\n", nrow(vertex_results), fmt_secs(last_runtime()$secs),
            last_runtime()$secs * p$n_cores / nrow(vertex_results)))
vertex_results <- merge(elements, vertex_results, by = "element_id", sort = TRUE)
vertex_results$p_fx_fdr <- stats::p.adjust(vertex_results$p_fx, method = "fdr")
head(vertex_results[, c("element_id", "vertex", "name", "edf", "F_fx", "p_fx_fdr", "delta_adj_rsq", "rate_8_22", "late_fraction", "age_fastest")])
```

### Repeat sessions, at one vertex

CovBat and the vertex-wise GAM treat repeat sessions as independent. A GAMM with a
subject random intercept (`gamm4`) is the honest alternative for the model, and
longitudinal ComBat (the `longCombat` package) for the harmonization. The GAMM is far
slower than a GAM, so the report fits it at the area-`r top_region` vertex only, with
site as a covariate, and gives up after two minutes.

```{r vertex-gamm}
if (have_gamm4) {
  d_long <- d_demo
  d_long$subject <- factor(d_long$subject)
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  gamm_fit <- tryCatch({
    setTimeLimit(elapsed = 120, transient = TRUE)
    gamm4::gamm4(f_demo, random = ~ (1 | subject), data = d_long, REML = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) e)
  setTimeLimit(elapsed = Inf)
  if (inherits(gamm_fit, "error")) {
    cat("The GAMM did not finish within 2 minutes at one vertex; skipped. (", conditionMessage(gamm_fit), ")\n")
  } else {
    nd_gamm <- typical_newdata(d_long, names(nd_demo))
    deriv_gamm <- smooth_derivative(gamm_fit$gam, nd_gamm)
    cat(sprintf("GAMM at one vertex took %s; smooth edf = %.2f (GAM: %.2f); mean slope 8-22 = %.1f microns/yr (GAM: %.1f)\n",
                fmt_secs(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")),
                summary(gamm_fit$gam)$s.table[1, "edf"], summary(fit_demo)$s.table[1, "edf"],
                1000 * mean(deriv_gamm$derivative[deriv_gamm$Age >= 8 & deriv_gamm$Age <= 22]),
                1000 * mean(deriv_demo$derivative[deriv_demo$Age >= 8 & deriv_demo$Age <= 22])))
  }
}
```

## 10. Does the result match the literature?

```{r parcel-summary}
q <- function(x, pr) unname(stats::quantile(x, pr, na.rm = TRUE))
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(vertex_results, vertex_results$name), function(v) {
  data.frame(name = v$name[1], hemi = v$hemi[1], region = v$region[1], sa_rank = v$sa_rank[1],
             vertices = sum(!is.na(v$late_fraction)),
             pct_fdr_sig = round(100 * mean(v$p_fx_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
             thickness_8 = median(v$pred_8, na.rm = TRUE),
             rate_8_22 = median(v$rate_8_22, na.rm = TRUE),
             pct_per_yr_8_22 = median(100 * v$rate_8_22 / v$pred_8, na.rm = TRUE),
             rate_8_14 = median(v$rate_8_14, na.rm = TRUE),
             rate_14_22 = median(v$rate_14_22, na.rm = TRUE),
             late_fraction = median(v$late_fraction, na.rm = TRUE),
             late_fraction_q25 = q(v$late_fraction, 0.25),
             late_fraction_q75 = q(v$late_fraction, 0.75),
             age_fastest = median(v$age_fastest, na.rm = TRUE),
             thinning_until = median(v$thinning_until, na.rm = TRUE),
             delta_adj_rsq = median(v$delta_adj_rsq, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
summ <- summ[order(summ$sa_rank, summ$hemi), ]
rownames(summ) <- NULL
summ_print <- summ
for (col in c("rate_8_22", "rate_8_14", "rate_14_22")) summ_print[[col]] <- round(1000 * summ_print[[col]], 1)
names(summ_print) <- sub("^rate_", "um_per_yr_", names(summ_print))
for (col in c("thickness_8", "pct_per_yr_8_22", "late_fraction", "late_fraction_q25", "late_fraction_q75")) summ_print[[col]] <- round(summ_print[[col]], 2)
summ_print$delta_adj_rsq <- round(summ_print$delta_adj_rsq, 4)
summ_print

if (nrow(summ) > 2) {
  rho_late <- stats::cor(summ$sa_rank, summ$late_fraction, method = "spearman")
  rho_age <- stats::cor(summ$sa_rank, summ$age_fastest, method = "spearman")
  cat(sprintf("\nSpearman correlation with S-A rank across %d parcel(s): late fraction rho = %.2f, age of fastest thinning rho = %.2f (both expected positive)\n",
              nrow(summ), rho_late, rho_age))
}
cat(sprintf("All parcels thin between 8 and 22: %s. Earliest-maturing parcel (smallest late fraction): %s (expected: 3b). Latest: %s (expected: the highest rank, %s).\n",
            all(summ$rate_8_22 < 0), summ$region[which.min(summ$late_fraction)], summ$region[which.max(summ$late_fraction)], summ$region[which.max(summ$sa_rank)]))
```

```{r parcel-figures, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
curves$parcel <- factor(curves$region, levels = parcel_regions)
fig3 <- ggplot(curves, aes(Age, thickness, colour = parcel, linetype = hemi)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(aes(fill = parcel), shape = 21, colour = "black", size = 2, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = parcel_cols) + scale_fill_manual(values = parcel_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Predicted thickness (mm), parcel median", colour = "Parcel", linetype = "Hemisphere",
       title = "Fitted age trajectories by parcel") + theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
fig3
ggsave(file.path(p$out_dir, "fig3_parcel_trajectories.png"), fig3, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
fig4 <- ggplot(curves, aes(Age, 1000 * slope, colour = parcel, linetype = hemi)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(aes(fill = parcel), shape = 21, colour = "black", size = 2.2, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = parcel_cols) + scale_fill_manual(values = parcel_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Slope of the age curve (microns/year), parcel median", colour = "Parcel", linetype = "Hemisphere",
       title = "When each parcel thins: slope of the thickness-age curve") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
fig4 <- add_brain(fig4, x = 0.36, y = 0.58, w = 0.22, h = 0.32)
fig4
ggsave(file.path(p$out_dir, "fig4_parcel_slopes.png"), fig4, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
```

What to expect, from the literature. Shaw et al. (2008, *J Neurosci*) found that
primary sensory and motor cortex follow simple, early trajectories while association
cortex follows later and more drawn-out ones. Tamnes et al. (2017, *J Neurosci*),
studying 8–29-year-olds, found about 1% thinning per year, fastest in prefrontal and
parietal association cortex and slow in sensorimotor cortex. Sydnor et al. (2021,
*Neuron*) put these regional differences on one S-A axis along which association
cortex matures last. Together they predict what the slope-by-age figure should show:
area 3b (sensorimotor, low rank) thinning fastest in childhood and flattening by
mid-adolescence, prefrontal area 46 (association, high rank) still thinning in the
twenties, and a higher late fraction for 46 than for 3b.

## 11. Save the results locally

Results never go back to S3. They are written as CSVs, and the per-vertex table also
goes into the local store in ModelArray's own results layout, next to the scalars it
came from.

```{r write-results}
utils::write.csv(vertex_results, file.path(p$out_dir, "vertex_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(summ, file.path(p$out_dir, "parcel_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
numeric_cols <- vapply(vertex_results, is.numeric, logical(1))
writeResults(local_h5, df.output = vertex_results[, numeric_cols], analysis_name = "gam_thickness_sa_ladder")
ModelArray(local_h5, scalar_types = response_scalar, analysis_names = "gam_thickness_sa_ladder")
cat("Wrote", file.path(p$out_dir, "vertex_results.csv"), "\n      ", file.path(p$out_dir, "parcel_summary.csv"), "\n      ", local_h5, "\n")
```

## 12. Look at the maps in Connectome Workbench

The per-vertex results become a CIFTI dscalar on the fsLR-164k mesh: one map per
statistic at the analysed vertices, and parcel-wide maps that paint each parcel with
its median thinning rate and its S-A rank. Vertices that were not analysed are NaN.
Workbench needs surfaces to draw on; TemplateFlow publishes fsLR surfaces at 32k, which
are upsampled to 164k here, and a `.spec` file ties everything together.

```{r cifti-export}
if (!have_wb) {
  cat("Connectome Workbench (wb_command) was not found, so no CIFTI files were written.",
      "Install Workbench and put wb_command on your PATH (or set write_cifti = TRUE) to get them.\n")
} else {
  n_vertices <- length(labels$key)
  maps <- c("sAge_F", "sAge_neglog10_fdr_p", "rate_8_22_mm_per_yr", "late_fraction", "age_fastest",
            "parcel_median_late_fraction", "parcel_median_rate_8_22", "parcel_SA_rank")
  m <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_vertices, ncol = length(maps), dimnames = list(NULL, maps))
  i <- vertex_results$vertex
  m[i, "sAge_F"] <- vertex_results$F_fx
  m[i, "sAge_neglog10_fdr_p"] <- -log10(vertex_results$p_fx_fdr)
  m[i, "rate_8_22_mm_per_yr"] <- vertex_results$rate_8_22
  m[i, "late_fraction"] <- vertex_results$late_fraction
  m[i, "age_fastest"] <- vertex_results$age_fastest
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(summ))) {
    in_parcel <- labels$key == labels$table$key[labels$table$name == summ$name[k]]
    m[in_parcel, "parcel_median_late_fraction"] <- summ$late_fraction[k]
    m[in_parcel, "parcel_median_rate_8_22"] <- summ$rate_8_22[k]
    m[in_parcel, "parcel_SA_rank"] <- summ$sa_rank[k]
  }
  txt <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR164k.txt")
  utils::write.table(m, txt, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, na = "NaN")
  names_file <- file.path(p$out_dir, "map_names.txt")
  writeLines(maps, names_file)

  template <- cached_download("https://fcp-indi.s3.amazonaws.com/data/Projects/RBC/CCNP_FreeSurfer-Post/SHA256E-s3385504--99c174365d91c22508a0de725b40e19f8e6b572c6efd88dfcd681e392e187267.nii",
                              "template_fsLR164k.dscalar.nii")
  stopifnot(file.size(template) == 3385504)
  dscalar <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR164k.dscalar.nii")
  converted <- tryCatch({
    wb_run("-cifti-convert", "-from-text", txt, template, dscalar, "-reset-scalars"); TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (!converted) {
    # This Workbench build did not accept "NaN" tokens: use a sentinel and turn it into NaN with 0/0
    utils::write.table(m, txt, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, na = "-99999")
    tmp <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR164k_sentinel.dscalar.nii")
    wb_run("-cifti-convert", "-from-text", txt, template, tmp, "-reset-scalars")
    wb_run("-cifti-math", "(x > -90000) * x / (x > -90000)", dscalar, "-var", "x", tmp)
    unlink(tmp)
  }
  wb_run("-set-map-names", dscalar, "-name-file", names_file)
  cat("Wrote", dscalar, "with maps:", paste(maps, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

```{r cifti-display}
if (have_wb) {
  tf <- "https://templateflow.s3.amazonaws.com/tpl-fsLR"
  spheres <- list()
  for (h in c("L", "R")) {
    for (d in c("32k", "164k")) {
      spheres[[paste(h, d, "sphere")]] <- cached_download(sprintf("%s/tpl-fsLR_hemi-%s_den-%s_sphere.surf.gii", tf, h, d))
      spheres[[paste(h, d, "area")]] <- cached_download(sprintf("%s/tpl-fsLR_hemi-%s_den-%s_desc-vaavg_midthickness.shape.gii", tf, h, d))
    }
  }
  spec164 <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR164k.spec")
  if (file.exists(spec164)) unlink(spec164)
  for (h in c("L", "R")) {
    structure <- if (h == "L") "CORTEX_LEFT" else "CORTEX_RIGHT"
    for (surf in c("inflated", "midthickness")) {
      s32 <- cached_download(sprintf("%s/tpl-fsLR_den-32k_hemi-%s_%s.surf.gii", tf, h, surf))
      s164 <- file.path(p$out_dir, sprintf("fsLR164k_hemi-%s_%s.surf.gii", h, surf))
      if (!file.exists(s164)) {
        wb_run("-surface-resample", s32, spheres[[paste(h, "32k", "sphere")]], spheres[[paste(h, "164k", "sphere")]], "BARYCENTRIC", s164)
      }
      wb_run("-add-to-spec-file", spec164, structure, s164)
    }
  }
  wb_run("-add-to-spec-file", spec164, "INVALID", dscalar)

  # A 32k copy for people who have their own 32k surfaces (parcel borders lose one vertex ring to NaN)
  template32 <- file.path(p$cache_dir, "template_fsLR32k.dscalar.nii")
  if (!file.exists(template32)) {
    wb_run("-cifti-create-dense-scalar", template32, "-left-metric", spheres[["L 32k area"]], "-right-metric", spheres[["R 32k area"]])
  }
  dscalar32 <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR32k.dscalar.nii")
  wb_run("-cifti-resample", dscalar, "COLUMN", template32, "COLUMN", "ADAP_BARY_AREA", "CUBIC", dscalar32,
         "-left-spheres", spheres[["L 164k sphere"]], spheres[["L 32k sphere"]],
         "-left-area-metrics", spheres[["L 164k area"]], spheres[["L 32k area"]],
         "-right-spheres", spheres[["R 164k sphere"]], spheres[["R 32k sphere"]],
         "-right-area-metrics", spheres[["R 164k area"]], spheres[["R 32k area"]])
  spec32 <- file.path(p$out_dir, "results_fsLR32k.spec")
  if (file.exists(spec32)) unlink(spec32)
  for (h in c("L", "R")) {
    structure <- if (h == "L") "CORTEX_LEFT" else "CORTEX_RIGHT"
    for (surf in c("inflated", "midthickness")) {
      wb_run("-add-to-spec-file", spec32, structure, cached_download(sprintf("%s/tpl-fsLR_den-32k_hemi-%s_%s.surf.gii", tf, h, surf)))
    }
  }
  wb_run("-add-to-spec-file", spec32, "INVALID", dscalar32)

  cat("Open the results in Workbench with either of:\n\n")
  cat("  wb_view", spec164, "\n")
  cat("  wb_view", spec32, "\n\n")
  cat("Pick the map 'parcel_median_late_fraction' and the inflated surfaces.",
      "To render a saved scene to PNG without the GUI: wb_command -scene-capture-image <scene> 1 <out.png>\n")
}
```
